newsitem.title: USA: Gehl adopts shareholder rights plan.
newsitem.headline: Gehl adopts shareholder rights plan.

text.p: Gehl Co said Thursday its board of directors adopted a shareholder rights plan to protect shareholders and the company if efforts are made to gain control of the company in a manner that is not in the best interests of the company and all of its shareholders.
The plan was not adopted in response to any specific effort to acquire control of the company, and the board is not aware of any such effort, Gehl said in a statement.

The rights are designed to provide additional protection against abusive takeover tactics such as partial tender offers, selective open-market purchases and offers for all the shares of the company at less than full value or at an inappropriate time, Gehl said.

The rights will be exercisable only if a person or group acquires 15 percent or more of the company's common stock or announces a tender offer which would result in ownership by a person or group of 15 percent or more of the common stock.
Each right will initially entitle shareholders to buy one one-hundredth share of the company's Series A Preferred Stock at an exercise price of $55 per one one-hundredth share, subject to adjustment.
Gehl also said its directors are authorized to reduce the 15 percent thresholds to not less than 10 percent.
The rights will be issued to shareholders of record on June 16, 1997. The rights will expire on May 28, 2007.
Gehl makes capital goods equipment for the agricultural and light industrial and construction industries.
